input.portPlanDimension: missing, renamed, malformed, and unknown fields (msc2-port-plan.md line 187, first sub-item)
input.description: A config on disk carries a top-level key AppConfig.CodingKeys has never named -- e.g. written by a newer MSC 1 release, or a hand edit. AppConfig's init(from:)/encode(to:) are both hand-written against one fixed CodingKeys enum (source lines 614-868), not a catch-all [String: Any] dictionary.

expected.claim: The unrecognized field is silently absent from the file once it has round-tripped through one load_app_config -> save_app_config cycle; a sibling known field in the same object still decodes correctly.

contrastWith.opposingClaim: The *untyped* load_config/save_config primitive (operating on a bare serde_json::Value, not AppConfig) preserves a field it doesn't recognize across the same kind of round trip -- documented as a deliberate divergence in config_repository.rs's own module doc comment.

notes: Had no executable case anywhere before this step: config_lifecycle.rs's existing test proves the primitive's behavior, but nothing pinned what happens once that same JSON passes through the typed AppConfig schema P5.4-P5.6 built on top of it -- the two layers behave oppositely on purpose, and only the typed layer matches what a real MSC 1 install would observe, since ConfigManager.init always decodes into the AppConfig struct before ever calling save().
